claims.text: Peds dosing (viscous lidocaine label): > 3 y w normal lean body mass and development: max dose set by wt or age, eg, a 5-y-old weighing 50 lb → ≤ 75–100 mg (3.7–5 mL);
claims.quote: For children over 3 years of age who have a normal lean body mass and normal body development, the maximum dose is determined by the child’s weight or age. For example: in a child of 5 years weighing 50 lbs., the dose of lidocaine should not exceed 75 to 100 mg (3.7 to 5 mL of lidocaine).

claims.text: infants and < 3 y: measure accurately, ≤ 1.2 mL applied to the area w a cotton-tipped applicator;
claims.quote: For infants and in children under 3 years of age, the solution should be accurately measured and no more than 1.2 mL be applied to the immediate area with a cotton-tipped applicator.

claims.text: wait ≥ 3 h between doses; max four doses in 12 h.
claims.quote: Wait at least 3 hours before giving the next dose; a maximum of four doses may be given in a 12-hour period.

claims.text: Boxed warning: seizures, cardiopulm arrest and death in children under 3 years when ⍉given in strict adherence to dosing; generally ⍉for teething pain.
claims.quote: Postmarketing cases of seizures, cardiopulmonary arrest, and death in patients under the age of 3 years have been reported with use of Lidocaine Viscous 2% when it was not administered in strict adherence to the dosing and administration recommendations. In the setting of teething pain, Lidocaine Viscous 2% should generally not be used.
claims.locator: Boxed Warning: Life-threatening and fatal events in infants and young children

claims.text: ⍉food for 60 minutes after use in the mouth or throat: topical anesthesia may impair swallowing and raise aspiration risk.
claims.quote: the production of topical anesthesia may impair swallowing and thus enhance the danger of aspiration. For this reason, food should not be ingested for 60 minutes following use of local anesthetic preparations in the mouth or throat area.
